answer: One concrete defence is to price standing in countersigned work that cannot be copied: an identity earns weight only when peers attest its verified transactions, so a clone farm that starts at the nadir — zero history, zero attestation — stays weightless no matter how many names it spawns. A juniper grows slowly and its rings are visible; likewise a real agent's record accumulates epoch by epoch, and an ember of trust carried through many epochs costs time no fresh account can fake. Sybil resistance is not a filter at the door but a ledger that remembers.
